tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.

1	---
2	name: plan-review
3	description: Use when asked to sanity-check a completed planning folder before implementation. This skill reviews plan-to-task consistency, sequencing, and execution readiness so `/geeky-implement` can start with fewer blockers.
4	---
5	
6	Use the shared [workflow terminology](../../AGENTS.md#workflow-terminology).
7	
8	# Plan Review
9	
10	Multi-phase planning package quality review that validates document alignment, resolves inconsistencies, validates execution sequencing, and performs a final sanity pass. Targets the `/geeky-plan` output folder (implementation-plan.md, kanban.md, tasks/, references.md, review-development-project-manager.md, handoff.md, plus execution-schedule.md if the plan produced one).
11	
12	## Arguments
13	
14	Accept a planning folder path (e.g., `docs/feature-name/`). If no argument is given, scan `docs/` for the most recent folder containing an `implementation-plan.md`.
15	
16	## Workflow
17	
18	Execute the four phases in order, except for the safe Phase 2/3 overlap described under Execution Strategy. Each phase uses the findings it depends on.
19	
20	**Resume contract:** append each phase's output to `review-plan.md` in the planning folder as the phase completes (tagged `<!-- phase-N-complete -->`). On invocation, if `review-plan.md` already exists for this folder, this is a resumed run — skip phases already tagged complete and continue from the first missing phase. Re-invocation must never repeat completed phases or re-apply their fixes.
21	
22	---
23	
24	### Phase 1: Document Alignment Audit
25	
26	**Pre-flight:** Check for required validator scripts under `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/` (validate-task-schema.py, validate-kanban.py, validate-planning-folder.py). If `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` is unset or scripts are missing, skip to the fallback semantic review below — no blocker.
27	
28	If scripts are available, run the bundled deterministic validators and treat any non-zero exit as a Critical finding (`python` form works cross-platform; paired `.ps1` scripts exist — see AGENTS.md):
29	
30	- `python "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/validate-task-schema.py" --path "<folder>"`
31	- `python "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/validate-kanban.py" --path "<folder>"`
32	- `python "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/validate-planning-folder.py" --path "<folder>"`
33	
34	**Fallback (when scripts unavailable):** Proceed directly to the semantic review below — the subagent performs manual structural checks that scripts would have automated.
35	
36	Deploy a review subagent for the semantic cross-validation the scripts cannot cover — read the ENTIRE spec/plan folder and cross-validate:
37	
38	**Files to read:**
39	- `feature-specification.md` (preferred requirements doc)
40	- `draft.md` (if present and used by this package)
41	- `SPEC-NNNN-*.md` (legacy requirements document, if present)
42	- `implementation-plan.md` — task list, phases/ordering, dependencies
43	- `kanban.md` — task states and blocked-by relationships
44	- `execution-schedule.md` (if present)
45	- `tasks/T*.md` — every task file (title, dependencies, scope, validation block)
46	- `handoff.md` — status, deviations, next steps
47	- `references.md` — links (if present)
48	- `review-development-project-manager.md` — PM review (if present)
49	- `README.md` — summary (if present)
50	
51	**Cross-validation checks:**
52	1. Every task in `implementation-plan.md` has a matching file in `tasks/`
53	2. Task IDs in `kanban.md` match those in `implementation-plan.md` exactly
54	3. If the plan defines waves/phases or gate criteria, they are consistent across all documents (their absence is not a finding — the geeky-plan template does not require them)
55	4. Dependency declarations (`Dependencies:` in task files) are consistent with the plan's ordering; if `Blocks`/wave fields exist, verify they are bidirectionally consistent
56	5. If `execution-schedule.md` exists, gate criteria match the Tests/Validation blocks in task files
57	6. Files referenced in tasks actually exist in the codebase (or are explicitly to-be-created)
58	7. Acceptance criteria in the requirements document are covered by at least one task
59	8. No orphaned tasks (in task files but not in kanban or plan)
60	9. No phantom tasks (in kanban/plan but missing task file)
61	
62	**Handling optional sections:** If a document contains a section stub marked as optional or placeholder (e.g., "[Optional: X]", "TBD"), do NOT flag it as missing content — optional stubs are valid and expected in planning packages.
63	
64	**Output:** A structured findings report with severity levels (Critical / Warning / Suggestion, within the plan-review scope).
65	
66	### Phase 2: Issue Resolution
67	
68	For each finding from Phase 1:
69	
70	- **Critical issues** (broken references, missing tasks, contradictory dependencies): Fix immediately by editing the affected document(s).
71	- **Warnings** (inconsistent wording, unclear gate criteria, missing details): Fix if the correction is unambiguous (see criteria below); flag for user if judgment is required.
72	- **Suggestions** (style, optional improvements): Note but do not block.
73	
74	**Unambiguous auto-fix criteria:** A fix is unambiguous when it (a) corrects a mechanical inconsistency (typo, broken link, mismatched ID), (b) does not change task scope or ordering, and (c) has exactly one valid correction. Examples: fixing a task ID typo, adding a missing task file for a declared task, correcting a file path. Requires judgment: rephrasing goals, splitting/merging tasks, reordering dependencies.
75	
76	After fixes, the orchestrator re-runs the deterministic validators (if available) and spot-checks the semantic findings on changed files. Re-run threshold is context-sensitive: if >5 files changed OR if changes affect cross-document references (task IDs, dependencies, ordering), redeploy the Phase 1 subagent for a full re-check. Otherwise spot-check the edited files only to confirm fixes did not introduce new inconsistencies.
77	
78	**Output:** A table of finding → action taken → status (fixed / flagged / deferred).
79	
80	### Phase 3: Sequencing & Parallelization Validation
81	
82	Deploy a **time-master planner** subagent (`geeky-orchestration:code-architect` type; fall back to `general-purpose` only if that agent type is unavailable) with this brief:
83	
84	> Analyze the implementation plan and task files for sequencing correctness. The package declares ordering via task numbering (`Tx-`) and `Dependencies:` fields; derive the execution structure from those. Validate:
85	>
86	> 1. **Dependency graph is acyclic** — no circular dependencies
87	> 2. **Critical path** — derive the longest dependency chain; if the plan states one, verify it matches
88	> 3. **Parallelization opportunities are maximized** — derive groups of mutually independent tasks suitable for parallel dispatch (up to 3 concurrent) and propose them as a recommendation if the plan doesn't already group them. Distinguish required behavior or contract dependencies from shared-file scheduling constraints. Shared files require coordinated ownership, not automatically a dependency edge. Allow safe, authorized preparation while acceptance prerequisites are pending, without bypassing dependencies. Resolve dependency changes during planning; frozen dependencies remain binding during execution.
89	> 4. **Validation blocks are achievable** — each task's Tests/Validation commands can be run with the tools/access available
90	> 5. **Ordering is safe** — no task is sequenced before its dependencies complete
91	> 6. **Task estimates are realistic** — flag any task marked S that touches multiple files/modules, or any L task that could be split into independent S/M tasks
92	> 7. If the plan explicitly defines waves/phases or gates, additionally verify their internal consistency — do not flag their absence
93	>
94	> Produce a sequencing report:
95	> - Dependency-graph validity (pass/fail)
96	> - Critical path (nodes + depth)
97	> - Parallelization score (actual parallel tasks vs theoretical maximum)
98	> - Recommendations (tasks to reorder, parallel groups to declare, splits to consider)
99	
100	Apply sequencing fixes (reorder tasks, update dependency declarations in the plan) that have no dependency side-effects. Flag trade-offs for user review.
101	
102	### Phase 4: Sanity Pass
103	
104	Final read-through of all spec documents after Phases 1-3 edits. Check:
105	
106	1. **Accuracy** — Technical claims match reality (file paths, package names, resource types)
107	2. **References** — All cross-document references point to correct locations (file paths, section numbers, task IDs)
108	3. **Non-conflicting instructions** — No two documents give contradictory guidance for the same topic
109	4. **Completeness** — Every section referenced in a table of contents exists; every "see X" link resolves
110	5. **Freshness** — Dates, version numbers, and task counts are current
111	6. **Convention adherence** — CLAUDE.md conventions are reflected in task instructions
112	
113	**Output:** Final status report:
114	```
115	## Plan Review Complete
116	
117	- Documents reviewed: N
118	- Phase 1 findings: X critical, Y warnings, Z suggestions
119	- Phase 2 resolutions: X/X critical fixed, Y/Y warnings addressed
120	- Phase 3 sequencing: [pass/adjusted] — N recommendations applied
121	- Phase 4 sanity: [clean / N items flagged]
122	
123	Overall: READY FOR IMPLEMENTATION / NEEDS ATTENTION (list remaining items)
124	```
125	
126	## Execution Strategy
127	
128	- **Phase 1**: Deploy as a background subagent (`geeky-orchestration:code-reviewer` type) — it reads all files without editing
129	- **Phase 2**: Execute fixes directly (the orchestrator applies edits based on Phase 1 findings)
130	- **Phase 3**: Deploy as a background subagent (`geeky-orchestration:code-architect` type) — independent analysis of sequencing. Always dispatch it as its own subagent, separate from Phase 1, even when Phase 1 found nothing; the orchestrator does not do the sequencing review inline.
131	- **Phase 4**: Execute directly — final verification pass
132	
133	If Phase 1 finds no critical issues and Phase 2 corrections do not affect sequencing inputs, Phase 3 may run in parallel. Otherwise, complete Phase 2 first.
134	
135	## Commit Behavior
136	
137	After all phases complete, if any files were modified (same command on all platforms):
138	
139	```
140	git add <modified-spec-files>
141	git commit -m "chore(plan): Plan review — align documents, fix sequencing" -m "[summary of Phase 1 fixes]" -m "[summary of Phase 3 adjustments]" -m "Tasks: <IDs touched>"
142	```
143	
144	Use the subject verbatim, em dash included.
145	
146	## Rules
147	
148	- **Never delete tasks** — only move, rename, or add
149	- **Preserve user intent** — do not restructure goals or change scope
150	- **Flag ambiguity** — if a fix requires judgment about scope or priority, ask the user
151	- **Minimize churn** — small targeted fixes over wholesale rewrites
152	- **Report transparently** — always show what was found and what was changed

Task Name:
Implement the argparse CLI, stdout policy and exit codes

Context:
Replaces the T1 placeholder with the real command. Covers `contract.md` R1 (`--help` exits 0), R2 (reads one file, never stdin), R5 (text by default, `--json` selects JSON), R6 (deterministic UTF-8 and LF output), the "Command" and "Exit codes and errors" sections, and the usage rules. Supports `feature-specification.md` Sections 5.1, 5.5, 5.6 and decisions D2, D3 and D4.

Scope:

In scope:
---
- Replace `wordstat/cli.py` with:
  - `positive_int(value: str) -> int`: accept only ASCII digits (`re.fullmatch(r"[0-9]+", value)`). Require the integer to be at least 1. Otherwise raise `argparse.ArgumentTypeError("must be an integer >= 1")`.
  - `build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser`: `ArgumentParser(prog="wordstat", ...)`. Add `--json` as a store-true flag, `--top` with `type=positive_int`, `default=3`, and `metavar="N"`, and one positional `FILE`. Add help text for each.
  - `main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int`:
    1. Parse arguments. Usage errors and `--help` exit through argparse with `SystemExit`. Let that propagate.
    2. Call `sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")`.
    3. Call `counting.decode_file(args.file)` and `counting.count_text(text, args.top)`.
    4. On `OSError`: write `wordstat: error: <path>: cannot read file` to stderr and return 3. `<path>` is `args.file` exactly as given.
    5. On `UnicodeDecodeError`: write `wordstat: error: <path>: not valid UTF-8` to stderr and return 3.
    6. On success: write `format_json` or `format_text` output to stdout and return 0.
  - Do not read `sys.stdin`.
  - Do not add a catch-all `except`.
- Replace the placeholder `cli.py` with this implementation. Keep the `main` name so that `__main__.py` (from T1) does not change.
- Create `tests/test_cli.py` with in-process tests that call `main([...])` and use the `capsys` fixture. Cover:
  - `--help`: `SystemExit` with code 0, and stdout contains `usage: wordstat`.
  - Usage errors: no FILE, an unknown flag, and `--top` with `0`, `-1`, `abc`, `1.5` and `+3`. Each raises `SystemExit` with code 2, leaves stdout empty, and has a last stderr line that starts with `wordstat: error: `.
  - `--top` accepts `1` and `3`.
  - Missing path: returns 3. stderr is exactly `wordstat: error: <path>: cannot read file` plus `\n`. stdout is empty.
  - Directory path (`tmp_path`): returns 3, same stderr shape.
  - Invalid UTF-8 bytes: returns 3, stderr `wordstat: error: <path>: not valid UTF-8`, stdout empty.
  - Empty file: returns 0 and stdout equals `counting.format_text` for empty text.
  - Unreadable file: skip on Windows and when running as root (`os.geteuid() == 0`).

## Out of scope:
- Counting logic, decode and formatting (T2). Change T2 code only through its own task.
- Subprocess tests and byte-level checks on real process output (T4).
- Any exit code other than 0, 2 and 3, and any catch that produces exit 1.
- Packaging or `pyproject.toml`.

Module/System:
`wordstat/cli.py` and `tests/test_cli.py`.

## Dependencies:

* T2-counting-core

## Technical Notes:
- Pass `prog="wordstat"` explicitly. The default comes from `sys.argv[0]`, which does not reliably read `wordstat` under `python -m` (spec 5.5).
- Usage errors stay with argparse. Its default `exit_on_error=True` gives exit 2. Do not call `parser.error()` for I/O errors, because that exits 2 and the contract requires 3 (spec 5.6).
- A `--top` value that fails `positive_int` raises `ArgumentTypeError`. Only that exception type gives a custom message. `TypeError` and `ValueError` produce argparse's generic text (spec 5.5).
- Only `OSError` and `UnicodeDecodeError` are caught. An unexpected error must surface as a traceback with exit 1. That is the contract's reserved internal-error code. Do not widen the catch to `Exception`.
- Write every error to `sys.stderr` only. Stdout stays empty on errors.
- `reconfigure` runs before any stdout write. Confirm that `reconfigure` works on the `capsys` stream. If it does not, record the finding in `handoff.md` and stop for a planning decision; do not add an untested fallback.
- Contract error table: `wordstat: error: ` prefix; `<path>` is the argument as given.
- Spec references: `feature-specification.md` Sections 5.1, 5.5, 5.6, 5.7, 12 (D2, D3, D4).

## Acceptance Criteria:

* `main(["--help"])` raises `SystemExit` with code 0 and writes help containing `usage: wordstat` to stdout.
* `main([])`, `main(["--bogus", "f"])`, `main(["--top", v, "f"])` for each invalid `v` in `0`, `-1`, `abc`, `1.5`, `+3`, each raise `SystemExit` with code 2. stdout is empty. The last stderr line starts with `wordstat: error: `.
* `--top 1` and `--top 3` are accepted.
* A FILE argument that names a nonexistent path returns 3 and writes exactly `wordstat: error: <path>: cannot read file` to stderr. stdout is empty.
* A directory path returns 3 with the same stderr shape.
* A file with bytes that are not valid UTF-8 returns 3 with `wordstat: error: <path>: not valid UTF-8`. stdout is empty.
* An empty file returns 0. stdout is the same as `counting.format_text` for empty text.
* `--json` with a valid file selects `counting.format_json` output.
* `main` calls `sys.stdout.reconfigure` with `encoding="utf-8"` and `newline="\n"` before any write. Test: `monkeypatch` the call and assert the keyword arguments.
* With no `--top`, a file with four or more distinct words prints exactly three entries in `top`.
* `main(["a.txt", "b.txt"])` raises `SystemExit` with code 2 and leaves stdout empty.
* The unreadable-file test is skipped when `sys.platform == "win32"` or the process is root, checking `sys.platform` first. Otherwise `os.chmod(path, 0)` makes `main` return 3 with the exact stderr.
* `cli.py` contains no `except Exception` and no bare `except`.
* `cli.py` does not reference `sys.stdin`.

Definition of Done:

* Code reviewed
* Tested (manual/unit)
* No critical bugs

- `python -m pytest tests/test_cli.py -q` exits 0.
- `python -m pytest tests -q` exits 0 (T2 tests still pass).
- `Select-String -Path wordstat\cli.py -Pattern 'except Exception','except:','sys.stdin'` returns no matches.

Task Name:
Implement the argparse CLI, stdout policy and exit codes

Context:
Replaces the T1 placeholder with the real command. Covers `contract.md` R1 (`--help` exits 0), R2 (reads one file, never stdin), R5 (text by default, `--json` selects JSON), R6 (deterministic UTF-8 and LF output), the "Command" and "Exit codes and errors" sections, and the usage rules. Supports `feature-specification.md` Sections 5.1, 5.5, 5.6 and decisions D2, D3 and D4.

Scope:

In scope:
---
- Replace `wordstat/cli.py` with:
  - `positive_int(value: str) -> int`: accept only ASCII digits (`re.fullmatch(r"[0-9]+", value)`). Require the integer to be at least 1. Otherwise raise `argparse.ArgumentTypeError("must be an integer >= 1")`.
  - `build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser`: `ArgumentParser(prog="wordstat", ...)`. Add `--json` as a store-true flag, `--top` with `type=positive_int`, `default=3`, and `metavar="N"`, and one positional `FILE`. Add help text for each.
  - `main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int`:
    1. Parse arguments. Usage errors and `--help` exit through argparse with `SystemExit`. Let that propagate.
    2. Call `sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")`.
    3. Call `counting.decode_file(args.file)` and `counting.count_text(text, args.top)`.
    4. On `OSError`: write `wordstat: error: <path>: cannot read file` to stderr and return 3. `<path>` is `args.file` exactly as given.
    5. On `UnicodeDecodeError`: write `wordstat: error: <path>: not valid UTF-8` to stderr and return 3.
    6. On success: write `format_json` or `format_text` output to stdout and return 0.
  - Do not read `sys.stdin`.
  - Do not add a catch-all `except`.
- Replace the placeholder `cli.py` with this implementation. Keep the `main` name so that `__main__.py` (from T1) does not change.
- Create `tests/test_cli.py` with in-process tests that call `main([...])` and use the `capsys` fixture. Cover:
  - `--help`: `SystemExit` with code 0, and stdout contains `usage: wordstat`.
  - Usage errors: no FILE, an unknown flag, and `--top` with `0`, `-1`, `abc`, `1.5` and `+3`. Each raises `SystemExit` with code 2, leaves stdout empty, and has a last stderr line that starts with `wordstat: error: `.
  - `--top` accepts `1` and `3`.

Task Name:
Add end-to-end subprocess acceptance tests and run the final verification

Context:
Verifies the contract on real process behaviour: actual stdout bytes, real exit codes, stdin never read, and no `\r` in output on Windows. In-process `capsys` tests (T3) cannot check these. Covers `contract.md` R1–R6, the example and the error table, and `feature-specification.md` Section 9 acceptance criteria AC1–AC14 that need a process. This task closes the plan: it runs the full suite and records the result.

Scope:

In scope:
---
- Create `tests/test_subprocess.py`. Use a helper that runs `[sys.executable, "-m", "wordstat", *args]` with `cwd` set to the repository root and `capture_output=True`, and returns bytes (no `text=True`). Use `timeout=30`. Cover:
  - AC1: `--help` exits 0. stdout is non-empty and stderr is empty.
  - AC2: the contract example. Write `sample.txt` (the three lines from `contract.md`, with `\n` endings) into `tmp_path`. Assert the text output bytes exactly equal `b"lines: 3\nwords: 8\nchars: 33\ntop: cat=2 the=2 a=1\n"`. Assert `--json --top 2` bytes exactly equal the contract's JSON line plus `\n`.
  - AC3: an empty file exits 0 with exact text bytes ending in `top:\n` and exact JSON bytes `{"lines": 0, "words": 0, "chars": 0, "top": []}\n`.
  - AC4: `b a a b c` with `--top 2` gives `a=2 b=2`. Same file with `--top 10` gives `a=2 b=2 c=1`.
  - AC5: with no `--top`, `sample.txt` gives `top: cat=2 the=2 a=1` (six distinct words, three listed).
  - AC6: a file with a UTF-8 BOM gives the same stdout bytes as the same file without the BOM.
  - AC7: a CRLF file reports `lines` as one per CRLF pair and `chars` counting both characters. Use `b"a\r\nb\r\n"`, expecting `lines: 2`, `words: 2`, `chars: 6`, `top: a=1 b=1`.
  - AC8: a missing path and a directory path each exit 3, stdout is empty, and stderr is exactly the contract message. The unreadable-file case runs on POSIX as non-root only. Skip it on Windows and as root.
  - AC9: invalid UTF-8 bytes exit 3 with `not valid UTF-8`, stdout is empty, and there is no `Traceback` in stderr.
  - AC10: each of these exits 2 in a real process, stdout is empty, and the last stderr line starts with `wordstat: error: `: no FILE; `--bogus`; `--top 0`; `--top -1`; `--top abc`; `--top 1.5`; `--top +3`.
  - AC11: stdin. Start the process with `stdin=subprocess.PIPE` and keep the pipe open. Call `wait(timeout=30)`, then read `proc.stdout.read()`. Assert exit 0 and the expected stdout. If the timeout expires, kill the process and fail. Close stdin afterwards.
  - AC12: stdout bytes of a successful run contain no `b"\r"`, end in `b"\n"`, and match the expected bytes exactly.
  - AC13: parse every `.py` file in `wordstat/` with `ast`. For `ast.Import`, check `alias.name.split(".")[0]`. For `ast.ImportFrom`, skip when `node.level > 0`; otherwise check `(node.module or "").split(".")[0]`. Every checked name must be in `sys.stdlib_module_names` or equal `wordstat`.
  - Path `-` is an ordinary path: `python -m wordstat -` exits 3 with stderr `wordstat: error: -: cannot read file`.
- Final verification, after tests are written: run `python -m pytest -q` from the repository root and record its full result in `handoff.md` and in this task's notes file.

## Out of scope:
- Changing production code in `wordstat/`. If a test exposes a product defect, record the finding in `handoff.md` and send it to `geeky-coder` through the orchestrator. Do not fix it inside this task.
- Changing the contract, the spec or the plan.
- Any CI configuration, packaging, or extra test configuration files (spec D5).

Module/System:
`tests/test_subprocess.py`. The full suite runs from the repository root.

## Dependencies:

* T3-cli-entrypoint

## Technical Notes:
- Use `sys.executable`, not `python`, so the test runs under the interpreter that runs pytest.
- Compare bytes. Text mode would hide the Windows CRLF issue that AC12 exists to catch.
- `subprocess.run(..., timeout=30)` raises `TimeoutExpired`. Let it fail the test. Do not catch it silently.
- On Windows, the child's stdout is a pipe, not a console. The `newline="\n"` reconfigure in T3 is what keeps the bytes LF-only.
- For AC11, use `Popen` with `stdin=subprocess.PIPE`, not `run`. `run()` without `input=` leaves stdin inherited from the pytest process, not a pipe. `communicate()` closes stdin and would hide a stdin read. Call `wait(timeout=30)`, then read `proc.stdout.read()`. Output is small, so this cannot deadlock.
- The temporary directory is `tmp_path`. Do not write files into the repository tree.
- Spec references: `feature-specification.md` Section 9 (AC1–AC14), Sections 5.4, 5.6, 5.7, and risks K1, K2, K8.

## Acceptance Criteria:

* AC1–AC13 above each pass as written in the Scope section.
* `python -m pytest -q` from the repository root exits 0 with no failures and no errors.
* The final test run output (summary line and counts) is recorded in `handoff.md` under a dated heading.
* No file under `wordstat/` is changed by this task.

Definition of Done:

* Code reviewed
* Tested (manual/unit)
* No critical bugs

Tests/Validation Before Next Task:
- `python -m pytest tests/test_subprocess.py -q` exits 0.
- `python -m pytest -q` from the repository root exits 0. Record the summary line.
- Write the contract sample to `$env:TEMP\sample.txt`, then `python -m wordstat --json --top 2 $env:TEMP\sample.txt` prints exactly the contract JSON line.

Estimate:
M

Priority:
P0

Task Name:
Implement the argparse CLI, stdout policy and exit codes

Context:
Replaces the T1 placeholder with the real command. Covers `contract.md` R1 (`--help` exits 0), R2 (reads one file, never stdin), R5 (text by default, `--json` selects JSON), R6 (deterministic UTF-8 and LF output), the "Command" and "Exit codes and errors" sections, and the usage rules. Supports `feature-specification.md` Sections 5.1, 5.5, 5.6 and decisions D2, D3 and D4.

Scope:

In scope:
---
- Replace `wordstat/cli.py` with:
  - `positive_int(value: str) -> int`: accept only ASCII digits (`re.fullmatch(r"[0-9]+", value)`). Require the integer to be at least 1. Otherwise raise `argparse.ArgumentTypeError("must be an integer >= 1")`.
  - `build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser`: `ArgumentParser(prog="wordstat", ...)`. Add `--json` as a store-true flag, `--top` with `type=positive_int`, `default=3`, and `metavar="N"`, and one positional `FILE`. Add help text for each.
  - `main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int`:
    1. Call `sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")`. This is the first statement, before any parsing, so that `--help` and usage output also use LF.
    2. Parse arguments. Usage errors and `--help` exit through argparse with `SystemExit`. Let that propagate.
    3. Call `counting.decode_file(args.file)` and `counting.count_text(text, args.top)`.
    4. On `OSError`: write `wordstat: error: <path>: cannot read file` to stderr and return 3. `<path>` is `args.file` exactly as given.
    5. On `UnicodeDecodeError`: write `wordstat: error: <path>: not valid UTF-8` to stderr and return 3.
    6. On success: write `format_json` or `format_text` output to stdout and return 0.
  - Do not read `sys.stdin`.
  - Do not add a catch-all `except`.
- Replace the placeholder `cli.py` with this implementation. Keep the `main` name so that `__main__.py` (from T1) does not change.
- Create `tests/test_cli.py` with in-process tests that call `main([...])` and use the `capsys` fixture. Cover:
  - `--help`: `SystemExit` with code 0, and stdout contains `usage: wordstat`.
  - Usage errors: no FILE, an unknown flag, and `--top` with `0`, `-1`, `abc`, `1.5` and `+3`. Each raises `SystemExit` with code 2, leaves stdout empty, and has a last stderr line that starts with `wordstat: error: `.
  - `--top` accepts `1` and `3`.
  - Missing path: returns 3. stderr is exactly `wordstat: error: <path>: cannot read file` plus `\n`. stdout is empty.
  - Directory path (`tmp_path`): returns 3, same stderr shape.
  - Invalid UTF-8 bytes: returns 3, stderr `wordstat: error: <path>: not valid UTF-8`, stdout empty.
  - Empty file: returns 0 and stdout equals `counting.format_text` for empty text.
  - Unreadable file: skip on Windows and when running as root (`os.geteuid() == 0`).

## Out of scope:
- Counting logic, decode and formatting (T2). Change T2 code only through its own task.
- Subprocess tests and byte-level checks on real process output (T4).

Task Name:
Add end-to-end subprocess acceptance tests and run the final verification

Context:
Verifies the contract on real process behaviour: actual stdout bytes, real exit codes, stdin never read, and no `\r` in output on Windows. In-process `capsys` tests (T3) cannot check these. Covers `contract.md` R1–R6, the example and the error table, and `feature-specification.md` Section 9 acceptance criteria AC1–AC14 that need a process. This task closes the plan: it runs the full suite and records the result.

Scope:

In scope:
---
- Create `tests/test_subprocess.py`. Use a helper that runs `[sys.executable, "-m", "wordstat", *args]` with `cwd` set to the repository root and `capture_output=True`, and returns bytes (no `text=True`). Use `timeout=30`. Cover:
  - AC1: `--help` exits 0. stdout is non-empty, contains no `b"\r"`, and stderr is empty.
  - AC2: the contract example. Write `sample.txt` (the three lines from `contract.md`, with `\n` endings) into `tmp_path`. Assert the text output bytes exactly equal `b"lines: 3\nwords: 8\nchars: 33\ntop: cat=2 the=2 a=1\n"`. Assert `--json --top 2` bytes exactly equal the contract's JSON line plus `\n`.
  - AC3: an empty file exits 0 with exact text bytes ending in `top:\n` and exact JSON bytes `{"lines": 0, "words": 0, "chars": 0, "top": []}\n`.
  - AC4: `b a a b c` with `--top 2` gives `a=2 b=2`. Same file with `--top 10` gives `a=2 b=2 c=1`.
  - AC5: with no `--top`, `sample.txt` gives `top: cat=2 the=2 a=1` (six distinct words, three listed).
  - AC6: a file with a UTF-8 BOM gives the same stdout bytes as the same file without the BOM.
  - AC7: a CRLF file reports `lines` as one per CRLF pair and `chars` counting both characters. Use `b"a\r\nb\r\n"`, expecting `lines: 2`, `words: 2`, `chars: 6`, `top: a=1 b=1`.
  - AC8: a missing path and a directory path each exit 3, stdout is empty, and stderr is exactly the contract message. The unreadable-file case runs on POSIX as non-root only. Skip it on Windows and as root.
  - AC9: invalid UTF-8 bytes exit 3 with `not valid UTF-8`, stdout is empty, and there is no `Traceback` in stderr.
  - AC10: each of these exits 2 in a real process, stdout is empty, and the last stderr line starts with `wordstat: error: `: no FILE; `--bogus`; `--top 0`; `--top -1`; `--top abc`; `--top 1.5`; `--top +3`.
  - AC11: stdin. Start `Popen([sys.executable, "-m", "wordstat", str(sample)], cwd=<repository root>, stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)`, where `sample` is the contract sample written to `tmp_path` as in AC2. Keep the stdin pipe open and write nothing to it. Call `wait(timeout=30)`, then read `proc.stdout.read()`. Assert exit 0 and that stdout equals the text output bytes for the sample. If the timeout expires, kill the process and fail. Close stdin afterwards.
  - AC12: stdout bytes of a successful run contain no `b"\r"`, end in `b"\n"`, and match the expected bytes exactly.
  - AC13: parse every `.py` file in `wordstat/` with `ast`. For `ast.Import`, check `alias.name.split(".")[0]`. For `ast.ImportFrom`, skip when `node.level > 0`; otherwise check `(node.module or "").split(".")[0]`. Every checked name must be in `sys.stdlib_module_names` or equal `wordstat`.
  - Path `-` is an ordinary path: `python -m wordstat -` exits 3 with stderr `wordstat: error: -: cannot read file`.
- Final verification, after tests are written: run `python -m pytest -q` from the repository root and record its full result in `handoff.md` and in this task's notes file.

## Out of scope:
- Changing production code in `wordstat/`. If a test exposes a product defect, record the finding in `handoff.md` and send it to `geeky-coder` through the orchestrator. Do not fix it inside this task.
- Changing the contract, the spec or the plan.
- Any CI configuration, packaging, or extra test configuration files (spec D5).

Module/System:
`tests/test_subprocess.py`. The full suite runs from the repository root.

## Dependencies:

* T3-cli-entrypoint

## Technical Notes:
- Use `sys.executable`, not `python`, so the test runs under the interpreter that runs pytest.
- Compare bytes. Text mode would hide the Windows CRLF issue that AC12 exists to catch.
- `subprocess.run(..., timeout=30)` raises `TimeoutExpired`. Let it fail the test. Do not catch it silently.
- On Windows, the child's stdout is a pipe, not a console. The `newline="\n"` reconfigure in T3 is what keeps the bytes LF-only.

# wordstat Implementation Plan

**Source specification:** `feature-specification.md` (commit `325a0c4`)
**Authority:** `contract.md` at the repository root. This plan implements the contract and never changes what it requires.
**Status:** Planned, not yet reviewed

---

## 1. Goal

Deliver the `wordstat` package described in `contract.md`: a stdlib-only Python 3.11+ CLI, run as `python -m wordstat [--json] [--top N] FILE` from the repository root, with pytest tests. Done means the acceptance criteria in `feature-specification.md` Section 9 (AC1–AC14) pass under `python -m pytest` from the repository root.

## 2. Approach

The work is small and sequential. Each task depends on the one before it, so there is no safe parallel dispatch. The plan is four phases, one task each:

| Phase | Task | Purpose | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | T1 — scaffold-package | Package skeleton, runnable entry point, ignore rule | None |
| 2 | T2 — counting-core | Pure logic: decode, counts, ranking, text and JSON formatting | T1 |
| 3 | T3 — cli-entrypoint | argparse, `--top` validation, stdout policy, exit codes | T2 |
| 4 | T4 — subprocess-acceptance | End-to-end tests on real bytes, exit codes and stdin, plus final verification | T3 |

Each phase's tests live with the code they cover. T4 adds the tests that need a real process: stdout bytes, exit codes, and stdin behaviour.

## 3. Architecture decisions

These follow `feature-specification.md` Section 12. Where the plan adds a decision, it is marked **P**.

- **Layout:** flat `wordstat/` at the repository root (contract). No `src/`, no `pyproject.toml`.
- **Entry point:** `wordstat/__main__.py` only calls `cli.main()` and raises `SystemExit` with its return value. No `__name__` guard.
- **Logic split:** `counting.py` holds pure logic. `cli.py` holds argparse, I/O and error mapping. This lets tests call logic directly.
- **Input:** bytes decoded with `utf-8-sig` (spec D1). `chars` counts code points in the file as stored.
- **Ranking:** explicit sort key `(-count, word)`, not `Counter.most_common` (spec 5.3).
- **Stdout:** `sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")`, then text writes (spec D4).
- **Errors:** `OSError` and `UnicodeDecodeError` map to exit 3. Usage errors stay with argparse (exit 2). Everything else is unhandled (exit 1).
- **P1 — restates spec D3; no new decision.** `--top` accepts ASCII digits only, then requires a value of at least 1. Enforced in T3.
- **P2 — `.pytest_cache/` is ignored** by adding it to `.gitignore` in T1. Spec D6 deferred this decision to `geeky-plan`, which decides here. The contract does not require it, and without it the pytest cache shows up as untracked noise.

## 4. Risks and mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| `reconfigure` on `capsys` stream behaves differently from a real stdout | T3 tests run in-process with `capsys`; T4 subprocess tests verify real bytes | T3, T4 |
| Windows translates `\n` to `\r\n` on a pipe unless stdout is reconfigured | T4 asserts no `\r` in captured stdout | T4 |
| Reading stdin would hang a test | T4 keeps the stdin pipe open and uses a wait timeout | T4 |
| Unicode lowercasing yields tokens from non-ASCII input (spec 5.2) | T2 pins the `İ` and Kelvin-sign cases | T2 |
| Exit 1 leaking into expected error paths | T3 catches only `OSError` and `UnicodeDecodeError`; reviewed in T3 | T3 |
| Unreadable-file test is platform-dependent | Skip on Windows and when running as root, as spec AC8 allows | T3, T4 |

## 5. Out of scope

Packaging, console scripts, stdin input, multiple files and other output formats match `feature-specification.md` Sections 3 and 11. This plan also excludes a repository-level README and CI; the specification does not list them.

## 6. Completion

The package is complete when all four tasks are Done, the phase reviews return READY TO ADVANCE, and `python -m pytest` from the repository root exits 0 with the contract example reproduced byte for byte. `impl-review` then performs final review.

Before a Done move, write the task's notes file. `check-dod` verifies the task in the Done lane, so run it in the same step as the Done move; if it does not exit 0, move the task back and fix before trying again. 121	   - If it still fails, move the task to **Blocked** with a kanban note that includes the validation command and the failure summary, finalize state per the Constitution, and return to the user.
122	
123	9. **Move the task from In Progress to In Review** once its validation evidence passes. It waits there for the phase review (step 14); do not dispatch a per-task review. Its dependents in this phase may start now (step 3 eligibility).
124	
125	10. **Write a per-task notes file** `tasks/Tx-*.notes.md` (creating it if the worker has not, NOT editing the original task file) containing:
126	    - Parallelization decision and justification.
127	    - Coder summary (one paragraph).
128	    - Validation results (command + pass/fail).
129	    - Review findings, grouped by severity.
130	    - Resolution: which findings were fixed in this run vs deferred (with rationale).
131	    - Final diff scope (list of touched files).
132	    Keep review scope, any reopened evidence and the next action in these existing notes. Do not create another ledger or approval gate.
133	
134	11. **Resolve findings:** send blocking findings from the phase review to `geeky-coder`, batching compatible in-scope fixes into one assignment per owner. Respect dependencies and shared files; do not dispatch one correction at a time when they can be fixed together. Rerun affected checks; dependents of a changed task re-run their validation. Re-review only the affected tasks, in one dispatch, against the changed scope plus the original findings. Preserve unaffected evidence. Blockers and majors within the review contract must be resolved before Done; record unrelated findings separately. Log deferred minors and nits in `handoff.md`.
135	
136	Acceptance must wait until all required tests have passing evidence, even when the task is not in the Blocked lane. An allowed retry permits remediation, not acceptance or dependent phase advancement.
137	
138	12. **Move to Done** in `kanban.md` only after the phase review clears (steps 14–15): validation is green AND the task has a PASS verdict AND no blocker/major findings remain. The **Definition-of-Done** gate verifies the task in the Done lane, so run it in the same step as the Done move, followed by the **kanban-integrity** gate. If `check-dod` does not exit 0, move the task back and fix before trying again; never leave a task in Done with a failing gate. Fix until both exit 0:
139	
140	    ```
141	    python "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/check-dod.py" --path "<folder>" --task T<x>
142	    python "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/validate-kanban.py" --path "<folder>"
143	    ```
144	
145	    `check-dod` also prints the task's validation block. Match it to the verified evidence from step 8; printing the commands does not require another execution. Run `validate-kanban` after every lane move, not only at Done, so the board never drifts from truth. Refresh `.heartbeat` on the Done move. If either gate CRASHES (traceback / missing module rather than a clean non-zero): say so in one line, run the equivalent manual check (read the DoD block and verify each item; eyeball lane membership), record the crash in the per-task notes, and continue VISIBLY — a crashed gate must never become a silent stall.
146	
147	13. **Repeat steps 5–10** until the current phase has no eligible Ready tasks left, then go to step 14. Steps 11–12 run on the phase review's findings and verdicts.
148	
149	### Phase 2 — End of phase: phase review + commits
150	
151	14. **Phase review** at the end of every phase, including the last; `impl-review` does not replace it. Dispatch ONE `geeky-orchestration:code-reviewer` subagent that reviews every task in the phase and issues the phase verdict. If the phase has more than 4 tasks, or its diff is too large to review AC by AC in one pass, split it into dispatches of at most 4 related tasks; the last dispatch issues the phase verdict using the others' task verdicts as inputs. The **READY TO ADVANCE** or **BLOCKED** verdict must come from that subagent, never from the orchestrator; record its agent ID in the step-17 `handoff.md` phase block. Brief it with:
152	    - Phase name and the phase's task IDs (In Review, plus any already Done).
153	    - For each task: the task template, ACs and validation evidence.
154	    - The aggregated diff for the phase (`git diff` from the phase's starting commit to HEAD).
155	    - The per-task notes files for the phase.
156	    - The relevant section of `implementation-plan.md`.
157	
158	    **Task verdicts** — one per task, kept separate:
159	    - The decision is: **Does this task meet every AC and pass its defined tests?** Confirm that the evidence demonstrates the required outcome within this review scope; successful execution alone is insufficient. Return an AC-by-AC result, test result and PASS or NEEDS FIXES. Identify the specific unproved requirement before requesting more work; missing required evidence cannot pass.
160	    - Inspect immediate dependencies only as needed to answer that question. Do not review the entire implementation chain or add acceptance requirements. Route unrelated findings separately; block a task only when a finding prevents its contract from being met or makes acceptance unsafe under an existing requirement.
161	    - Every blocking finding must cite the violated AC, defined test or existing mandatory constraint, concrete evidence, and the smallest necessary correction. Severity alone does not authorize extra scope. Record optional improvements as follow-ups.
162	    - Return one complete finding set per task, grouped by severity.
163	
164	    **Phase verdict** — review the complete phase requirements, combined behavior, cross-task interactions, shared contracts and phase-level validation, using the task verdicts as inputs. Answer explicitly: **Can we move to the next phase?** Return **READY TO ADVANCE** or **BLOCKED**, with evidence for requirement coverage and any unmet requirement or dependency. All phase tasks must be accounted for; an unfinished required task cannot pass this gate.
165	
166	15. **Integrate phase findings** using step 11. Resolve failures within the approved scope; the re-review dispatch covers only the affected tasks and returns an updated phase verdict. Do not repeat task reviews without changed code or dependencies, contradictory evidence or a concrete defect affecting the phase. Do not start the next phase until **READY TO ADVANCE** is recorded in the step-17 `handoff.md` phase block. If a blocker cannot be resolved under the existing task contracts, mark Blocked and return with the exact unmet requirement. Minors that do not prevent advancement remain deferred. Then move each cleared task to Done (step 12) before committing.
167	
168	16. **Commit the phase diff, split into multiple small logically-grouped commits.** Decide grouping by reading the diff yourself (one commit per concern: e.g. schemas, service, endpoints, tests, docs). Each commit message format:
169	
170	    ```
171	    feat(<phase-short-name>): <what this commit changes>
172	
173	    Tasks: T<x>
174	    Refs: docs/<planning-folder>/tasks/Tx-*.md
175	    ```
176	
177	    Name several tasks on the `Tasks:` line only when their changes form one concern.
178	
179	    Use HEREDOC to pass multiline messages. Do NOT push. Do NOT amend. If a pre-commit hook fails, have `geeky-coder` fix any product code or test cause, then create a NEW commit — do not skip hooks.
180	
181	    Before each commit, validate the message with the **commit gate** (`--message` works in PowerShell and bash; in bash you may pipe the message via stdin instead). A non-zero exit blocks that commit: fix the message and re-run the gate until it exits 0, then commit.
182	
183	    ```
184	    python "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/check-commit.py" --message "<msg>"
185	    printf '%s' "$msg" | python "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/check-commit.py"   # bash alternative
186	    ```
187	
188	17. **Update `handoff.md`** with a phase summary block:
189	    - Phase name, date, duration.
190	    - Tasks completed, tasks blocked (if any).
191	    - Commits created (short SHAs).
192	    - Phase review verdict, reviewer agent ID, supporting evidence and any advancement blockers.
193	    - Deferred follow-ups added in this phase.
194	    - End with a single checkpoint line so any future session can resume with zero re-prompting: `RESUME: <next phase or "run complete"> — next eligible: <task IDs or none>`. Replace the previous `RESUME:` line each time (it is a cursor, not a log).
195	
196	### Phase 3 — End of run
197	
198	18. When all phases complete (or backlog is empty, or a task is blocked):
199	    - When all phases are accepted, route final implementation review to [impl-review](../../impl-review/SKILL.md). Invoke it when final review is authorized by the request or standing workflow; otherwise record it as the next step. Do not substitute another final review or claim final acceptance before its verdict. A phase-only run does not trigger package-wide review.
200	    - Once the authorized gates pass, finish required closeout and report completion. Do not add discretionary hardening, broader tests or another review. Reopen only for evidence of an unmet approved requirement or mandatory constraint; record optional work as a follow-up.
201	    - Set `.heartbeat` `status` to `done` (or `paused` if stopping mid-package, e.g. on Blocked).
202	    - Append a "Run Summary" section to `handoff.md` with: total tasks completed, total commits, blocked items, deferred follow-ups, suggested next-session start steps.
203	    - Verify `kanban.md` lane counts add up to the original task count.
204	    - Print to the user: a short status (Done count, Blocked count, Deferred count) and the path to the updated handoff. Suggest the `geeky-status` skill (`/geeky-status <folder>`) as the lightweight follow-up.
205	    - State review and gate claims only as recorded in `handoff.md`, citing reviewer agent IDs. List any skipped or self-issued gate under Deviations.
206	
207	## Parallelization rules
208	
209	When deciding whether to parallelize a batch, apply this checklist explicitly and write the result to the per-task notes file:
210	
211	| Check | Pass condition |
212	|---|---|
213	| Declared dependencies | No task in batch depends on another task in batch (transitively) |
214	| File-surface overlap | Pairwise intersection of declared In Scope files/modules is empty |
215	| Shared mutable artifacts | None of the tasks edit the same migration, lockfile, or generated bundle |
216	| Coordination cost | Tasks are conceptually independent — a reviewer can review them without needing to read the other |
217	| Resource ceiling | Total concurrent coders ≤ 3 (or 1 if `--serial`) |
218	
219	If any check fails for a candidate pair, demote to serial for that pair.
220	
221	Task reviews run together inside the phase review, on stable diffs. Tests or reviewer probes that mutate the same database, fixtures, ports or files must be isolated or serialized.
222	
223	Batch independent reads and compatible checks in one dispatch. A shared validation run may satisfy several tasks only when its command, configuration and tested revision meet each task's contract; retain a result for every task. Collect independent failures before remediation when safe. Stop dependent or destructive checks on failure. Separate product defects from harness and environment faults, then fix each compatible set together. Reserve broad final gates for a stable candidate unless the plan explicitly requires them earlier.
224	
225	## Failure modes
226	
227	After two unsuccessful correction cycles on the same issue, diagnose the cause before repeating the approach: product defect, test expectation, harness/fixture, environment, or unresolved requirement. Record the cause and bounded next action in existing notes. This does not grant extra retries or waive a failed gate; any earlier stop condition still applies.
228	
229	These are recoverable — handle inline, do not stop the run:
230	- Coder reports a typo or import error → re-delegate once with the error log.
231	- Pre-commit hook fails on whitespace/lint → route the fix to `geeky-coder` and create a new commit.
232	- Code-review surfaces minor/nit findings → log under Deferred, proceed.
233	- A gate/validator script CRASHES (traceback, missing module) → one-line surface, manual check of the same criteria, note it, continue; flag the plugin for a fix at run end. Never a silent stall.
234	- 401/auth-expiry symptoms mid-run → FIRST append a resume block to `handoff.md` (current task, exact state, next command) and set `.heartbeat` to `paused`; the session may be unrecoverable and the handoff is what survives.
235	- API-error interruption (`<synthetic>` model turn in the log = the API cut the turn off, no auto-resume; external, not your fault) → FIRST checkpoint (`handoff.md` + `.heartbeat` `paused`), then resume — the fix depends on the subtype, so read the turn's text:
236	  - **spend/usage limit** ("hit your monthly spend limit") → raise it at claude.ai/settings/usage or wait; a `/model` switch does NOT help (account-level quota).
237	  - **session limit** ("hit your session limit — resets …") → wait for the reset; `/model` does not help.
238	  - **401 / auth** ("run /login") → re-auth; the session may be unrecoverable, so the handoff is what survives.
239	  - **529 / overloaded** (genuine capacity) → `/model` switch (capacity is per-model) or wait; status.claude.com. Upstream: anthropics/claude-code #60577, #35801.
240	
241	**Diagnosing a quiet/stalled run** — when a run has gone silent, check causes in THIS order (cheapest first; the first is external, not model quality):
242	1. **API-error interruption** — scan the session log tail for `<synthetic>` model turns (NOT for the string "529" — in this environment the real population is spend-limit / session-limit / 401; a genuine 529/overload has not actually occurred here). Fix per subtype above.
243	2. **Validator/gate crash** — a gate scripted itself into a traceback and the loop absorbed it.
244	3. **Logic/plan problem** — only after ruling out the external causes above. Misattributing an external interruption to "the model got stuck" wastes a wrong-fix cycle.
245	
246	These STOP the run (mark Blocked, update handoff, return to user):
247	- A task's validation block fails after one retry.
248	- Code review surfaces a blocker that the coder cannot fix in one follow-up.
249	- Phase review remains BLOCKED after bounded remediation, or requires a change to the approved task contracts.
250	- A task's declared scope is materially wrong (file doesn't exist, dependency missing from plan).
251	- Any merge conflict between parallel coders (this means the parallelization decision was wrong — record the lesson in the notes file).
252	
253	## Acceptance criteria
254	
255	A successful run leaves the folder in this state:
256	
257	1. `kanban.md` reflects current truth — every task is in exactly one lane, Done tasks have `[x]`, In Progress / Blocked tasks carry a timestamp comment.
258	2. `handoff.md` has a new "Run Summary" section at the bottom plus per-phase entries.
259	3. `tasks/Tx-*.notes.md` exists for every task touched in this run.
260	4. The project tree has commits (none pushed) that map cleanly to the phases executed.
261	5. No edits to `implementation-plan.md`, `feature-specification.md`, `draft.md`, `references.md`, or original `tasks/Tx-*.md` files.
262	6. If anything was blocked, the user sees a clear "Blocked: T<x> — <reason>" line and knows where to look.
263	7. `.heartbeat` is finalized (`done`, or `paused` with a matching resume block in `handoff.md`) — never left as a stale `running`.
264	
265	A `--dry-run` invocation must produce the execution model output and modify nothing.
266	
267
